question: Why do nurses champion routine immunization as a powerful tool in public health?

options.A: It transforms harmful chemical agents into harmless substances
options.B: It instantly cures patients who are already showing active symptoms
options.C: It completely destroys all environmental reservoirs of the pathogen
options.D: It makes potential hosts immune before they ever encounter the agent

explanation: Vaccines train the body's immune system ahead of time so it's ready to block the germ the very second it tries to enter!

question: How do pelvic floor exercises help patients recovering from GU cancer treatments?

options.A: They increase testosterone production in the testes
options.B: They strengthen muscles to help regain bladder control
options.C: They improve the filtration rate of the renal cortex
options.D: They prevent the recurrence of cancerous cell growth

explanation: Pelvic floor exercises (like Kegels) tone up the muscles supporting the bladder and urethra, which is a huge help for clients dealing with leakage after surgery.

question: Why is recording the exact date and vaccine type so important for community health?

options.A: It proves to patients that the nurse has good handwriting
options.B: It allows the clinic to calculate daily financial profits
options.C: It prevents missed appointments and avoids duplicate dosing
options.D: It stops vaccine manufacturers from making more doses

explanation: Good records help us track when the next dose is due and make sure patients don't get accidental double doses.

question: Why would a doctor choose a tracheostomy instead of keeping a breathing tube through the mouth long-term?

options.A: It completely stops any risk of getting an infection
options.B: It means you never have to clean around the site or use suction
options.C: It is much more comfortable and safer for long-term breathing support
options.D: It is much faster to do in an outdoor emergency

explanation: Having a tube taped through the mouth for weeks can damage the vocal cords and mouth. A tracheostomy provides a secure, comfortable airway right through the neck for patients who need long-term help.

question: Why might a high fever temporarily lower a male patient's sperm count?

options.A: White blood cells consume all available nutrients inside the seminiferous tubules
options.B: Higher body temperature disrupts the cool environment needed for healthy sperm development
options.C: Infections directly destroy mature sperm cells stored inside the urinary bladder
options.D: Fever causes the pituitary gland to permanently stop producing testosterone

explanation: Remember, sperm love cooler temperatures! A high fever raises the temperature in the scrotum, which temporarily pauses or slows down normal sperm production.

question: Why do you need to be extra careful with cleaning liquids on a smart bed?

options.A: Infection control policies do not apply to automated furniture
options.B: Standard hospital beds never require chemical disinfectants
options.C: Smart bed mattresses are made of disposable paper materials
options.D: Smart beds have electronic panels and crevices where liquid can damage components

explanation: Because of all the wires and electronic touchpads, you must clean carefully so liquid doesn't seep inside and break the bed.

question: What is the main reason behind conduction deafness?

options.A: Destruction of hair cells from loud music
options.B: Blocked transmission of sound waves to the inner ear
options.C: Damage to the auditory cortex in the brain
options.D: Degeneration of the vestibulocochlear nerve

explanation: Conduction deafness simply means a physical block—like earwax, fluid, or a stuck bone—is stopping sound waves from traveling smoothly inside.

question: Which of these statements is FALSE regarding legal accountability in drug administration?

options.A: A nurse is completely free from liability if a doctor wrote the incorrect order
options.B: A nurse can lose their nursing license for gross negligence in medication handling
options.C: A nurse is legally responsible for verifying every drug before giving it
options.D: A nurse must follow facility policies and state scope of practice laws

explanation: You can't just blame the doctor! Nurses share legal accountability and cannot blindly give a harmful drug just because it was prescribed.

question: Which complication involves dangerous pressure build-up inside an enclosed muscle compartment that cuts off blood supply?

options.A: Avascular necrosis
options.B: Fat embolism syndrome
options.C: Compartment syndrome
options.D: Osteomyelitis infection

explanation: Compartment syndrome occurs when swelling restricted by tight fascia compresses blood vessels and nerves, threatening limb survival. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h9)

question: Why is true primary nursing often difficult to practice in busy public Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and high nurse-to-patient ratios make 24-hour individual accountability hard to maintain.
options.B: Patients in Nigeria prefer seeing a different nurse every hour for variety.
options.C: Physicians in Nigerian hospitals handle all bedside nursing duties themselves.
options.D: Nigerian nursing councils legally forbid registered nurses from writing patient care plans.

explanation: Real talk: managing a packed ward with limited hands means nurses often have to focus on quick tasks rather than continuous one-on-one primary care.

question: Which of these actions is NOT a good recommendation for nurse-led STI prevention education?

options.A: Demonstrating the correct application of barrier methods
options.B: Discussing the schedule for routine screening and follow-up tests
options.C: Instructing patients on how to use chemical disinfectants vaginally
options.D: Explaining the importance of completing prescribed antibiotic courses

explanation: You nailed it! Douching and harsh chemicals actually harm natural protective barriers and raise the risk of infection. Never recommended!

question: A patient asks why taking gym steroids can cause infertility. How should you explain it?

options.A: Testosterone supplements cause the blood-testis barrier to permanently close off blood supply
options.B: External hormones trick the brain into stopping natural LH and FSH production, which shuts down sperm creation in the testes
options.C: High hormone levels cause the prostate gland to block the urethra completely
options.D: Anabolic steroids directly dissolve mature sperm stored inside the epididymis and vas deferens

explanation: When you put artificial testosterone into the body, the brain thinks, 'We have too much!' and stops making the hormones (LH and FSH) that tell the testes to make sperm.

question: What can happen if severe, constant pregnancy heartburn is left completely untreated?

options.A: Inflammation and damage to the lining of the esophagus
options.B: Permanent hardening of the muscular stomach walls
options.C: Complete blockage of the upper respiratory airway
options.D: Sudden loss of all maternal digestive enzymes

explanation: Constant acid wash irritates and damages the delicate lining of the food pipe over time, leading to inflammation.

question: A patient is fitted with a vaginal pessary for a uterine prolapse. What key instruction must the nurse include in her discharge teaching?

options.A: Leave the device in place permanently without removal.
options.B: Report any unusual discharge, odor, or discomfort promptly.
options.C: Expect the pessary to cure the prolapse within one week.
options.D: Avoid all physical activity while the device is in place.

explanation: You got it! Pessaries need careful monitoring. Any strange discharge or odor is a red flag that could mean irritation or infection, so the patient must report it right away.

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?

options.A: Post-infectious immunity
options.B: Secondary sepsis
options.C: Acute viral syndrome
options.D: Long COVID

explanation: Correct! 'Long COVID' is the term used when symptoms stick around long after the acute virus has cleared the body.

question: What is a very important safety step when caring for an elderly patient who just started a tranquilizer?

options.A: Checking blood glucose levels every two hours
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent nighttime urination
options.C: Encouraging immediate participation in heavy physical exercise
options.D: Implementing strict fall precautions due to sedation and dizziness

explanation: Sedatives make older adults feel dizzy and unsteady on their feet, so keeping them safe from accidental falls is a top nursing priority!

question: What happens if a patient starts eating a lot of fiber but forgets to drink enough water?

options.A: The patient will immediately develop severe watery diarrhea
options.B: Constipation can actually worsen because stool becomes dry and bulky
options.C: Kidney function will fail due to excess nutrient absorption
options.D: Fiber will pass through the body completely unchanged

explanation: Remember: fiber acts like a sponge! Without water, it cannot swell properly and will just form a hard, difficult lump in the gut.

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient right after placing a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Drink a full glass of water immediately to wash it down.
options.B: Lie flat on your back for at least one hour.
options.C: Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the pill is fully dissolved.
options.D: Chew the tablet quickly to help it enter the bloodstream.

explanation: Eating or drinking washes the medication away before it can absorb through the oral mucosa. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: Which of these is a key part of healthy sleep hygiene?

options.A: Consuming a large, heavy meal right before bedtime
options.B: Maintaining consistent sleep and wake times every day
options.C: Watching television in bed until falling asleep
options.D: Keeping the bedroom bright and warm throughout the night

explanation: Spot on! Waking up and sleeping at the same time daily helps train your body's internal clock (circadian rhythm), making sleep much more refreshing.

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to use nystatin oral suspension for mouth thrush?

options.A: Swallow the liquid immediately on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
options.B: Swish the liquid thoroughly around the mouth before swallowing it
options.C: Dilute the entire bottle in a glass of cold fruit juice and drink it fast
options.D: Gargle the liquid at the back of the throat and spit it out without swallowing

explanation: Correct! The medication needs time to touch all the infected spots in the mouth before it is swallowed down to coat the throat or gut.

question: A patient in Buck's extension says their heel feels like it is burning under the foam boot. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Inspect the skin under the boot for redness or pressure damage
options.B: Permanently cut off the traction straps without telling anyone
options.C: Add an extra weight to the rope to lift the heel higher
options.D: Administer a strong sleeping pill to help ignore the sensation

explanation: A burning feeling is an early warning sign of a pressure sore. Taking a quick look underneath can prevent a major wound!

question: Which of these practices is DANGEROUS and should be avoided when writing dosages?

options.A: Writing out the word 'units' instead of abbreviations
options.B: Using a leading zero before a decimal (0.5 mg)
options.C: Using a trailing zero after a whole number (e.g., 5.0 mg)
options.D: Checking unfamiliar doses in a drug handbook

explanation: Never use trailing zeros! If the decimal point gets smudged, 5.0 mg can easily look like 50 mg. Keep it simple and safe (just write 5 mg).

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

options.A: High fever accompanied by generalized body rash
options.B: Extreme weight gain within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: An abnormal heart murmur and breathing difficulty
options.D: Complete inability to pass any meconium stool

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood swirling through unclosed shunts creates extra sounds we hear as a murmur, and extra fluid can make the baby breathe a bit faster. You're learning real clinical skills! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: What is the primary cause of occupational lung diseases?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes without using a proper filter
options.B: Breathing in harmful workplace dusts and chemicals
options.C: Severe bacterial infections caught in the community
options.D: Inherited genetic defects of the respiratory tract

explanation: These conditions are directly caused by inhaling hazardous substances present in the work environment over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: What two main ingredients are combined in the scientific method?

options.A: Tradition and personal intuition
options.B: Gut feelings and unverified habits
options.C: Rational logic and empirical observation
options.D: Strict authority and superstition

explanation: Science brings together logical thinking and real, measurable sensory data to test ideas properly.

question: What is a crucial nursing responsibility during the recovery phase for a patient who survived severe asphyxia?

options.A: Stopping all vital sign measurements
options.B: Performing regular neurological checks
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise right away
options.D: Restricting all family visits indefinitely

explanation: Keeping a close eye on brain function with regular neuro checks lets you catch any delayed complications early on. Great nursing care!

question: A patient in labour shows severe moulding and the baby's heart rate is dropping. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the mother to push harder with every contraction to speed up birth
options.B: Wait another two hours to see if the cervix dilates any further on its own
options.C: Administer oxytocin infusion to strengthen contractions and force descent
options.D: Notify the doctor immediately and prepare for an emergency Caesarean section

explanation: When severe moulding meets a distressed baby heart rate, time is precious! Call the doctor right away and get ready for an emergency CS to save the day.

question: Which practice should nurses avoid when handling used injection needles?

options.A: Activating the safety device
options.B: Dropping it straight into a bin
options.C: Carrying it in a dedicated tray
options.D: Recapping the needle by hand

explanation: Recapping needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and should never be done. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why is eating a balanced diet important when managing chronic fatigue?

options.A: It stops the digestive system from producing inflammatory enzymes.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any physical rest during the day.
options.C: It prevents blood sugar swings that drain daily energy reserves.
options.D: It directly increases the number of red blood cells in the liver.

explanation: Exactly! Balanced meals keep blood sugar stable. Big sugar spikes and crashes only make fatigue worse, so steady food equals steady energy.

question: A patient is admitted with right-sided heart failure. Which physical sign is the nurse most likely to spot?

options.A: Flushed, warm skin and bounding pulses
options.B: Sudden high fever and severe headache
options.C: Bulging neck veins and swollen ankles
options.D: Clear lung sounds with no breathing trouble

explanation: Right-sided failure causes fluid to back up into the rest of the body. You'll often see this as swollen legs and distended neck veins!

question: Which of the following conditions is characterized by high lung pressure and the failure of fetal shunts to close properly after birth?

options.A: Congenital liver failure from the ductus venosus
options.B: Neonatal systemic hypotension
options.C: Placental abruption syndrome
options.D: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn

explanation: PPHN occurs when high pulmonary resistance persists, keeping fetal shunts open and starving the body of oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary job of the protein dystrophin in healthy skeletal muscle?

options.A: Transporting calcium ions out of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.B: Generating the electrical action potential along the sarcolemma
options.C: Linking the muscle cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix
options.D: Acting as the primary enzyme that breaks down glucose for energy

explanation: Dystrophin acts like a sturdy internal anchor, connecting the muscle cell's inner framework to its outer environment for stability during contractions.

question: You discover that a contaminated oxygen machine is spreading a bacterial infection in your ward. What is your very first action?

options.A: Wait until all patients finish their breathing treatments before cleaning
options.B: Rinse the exterior surface quickly with ordinary tap water
options.C: Leave the machine in place but place a warning sign on the wall
options.D: Remove the equipment from service for proper cleaning and sterilization

explanation: Safety first! Take the dirty equipment out of action immediately so no more patients are exposed while you arrange for proper sterilization.

question: A student nurse checks a drug's mechanism and possible side effects before giving it to a patient. Which historical role of nursing does this action reflect?

options.A: The nurse performing duties restricted only to senior physicians
options.B: The nurse relying solely on oral traditional folklore
options.C: The nurse acting as a primitive apothecary mixer from the Middle Ages
options.D: The nurse acting as an active safety barrier and clinical monitor

explanation: Modern nurses serve as the final safety check in medication administration, requiring them to understand drug actions and watch for adverse reactions before and after giving medication. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is mixed feeding (breast milk plus other foods or water) discouraged for infants exposed to HIV?

options.A: It damages the infant's immature gut lining and increases transmission risk.
options.B: It is too expensive for families living in rural communities.
options.C: It prevents the baby from ever developing taste preferences.
options.D: It causes immediate allergic reactions in all newborn infants.

explanation: Introducing other liquids or foods irritates the baby's gut wall, making it much easier for the HIV virus in breast milk to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: What are the three core parts of the famous epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Source, vector, and cure
options.B: Bacteria, virus, and parasite
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Infection, symptom, and recovery

explanation: Never forget the classic trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (the surroundings). You've got this memorized now!

question: Which nursing action directly attacks a biological germ inside a patient's body?

options.A: Screening building ventilation systems
options.B: Teaching mothers how to wash their hands
options.C: Administering a prescribed course of antibiotics
options.D: Ensuring proper disposal of community waste

explanation: Medicines like antibiotics go right inside the patient to fight off and destroy the invading bacteria. Simple and direct!

question: What important advice should a nurse give a heart failure patient about managing fluids at home?

options.A: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.B: Drink at least four liters of water every single morning
options.C: Weigh yourself daily and report sudden weight gains
options.D: Avoid all physical movement to save body water

explanation: Brilliant! Stepping on the scale every day is the easiest way for a patient to catch fluid buildup before it turns into breathing trouble.

question: Why do modern healthcare facilities promote a blame-free reporting culture for medication errors?

options.A: It encourages open reporting to identify system flaws and prevent future errors
options.B: It reduces the need for expensive hospital legal representation
options.C: It ensures that nurses never have to face consequences for careless mistakes
options.D: It speeds up the process of discharging patients from the hospital

explanation: When staff feel safe from unfair punishment, they report mistakes honestly, allowing the team to fix underlying system weaknesses. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: Which food group is the best natural source of dietary fiber to promote healthy bowel movements?

options.A: Fatty red meats and processed dairy products
options.B: Processed white bread and refined white rice
options.C: Fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
options.D: Clear sugary beverages and bottled juices

explanation: Plant-based foods and whole grains contain high amounts of natural fiber, which bulks stool and stimulates regular elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why should researchers be honest about study limitations in their published papers?

options.A: To trick reviewers into approving weak methodologies
options.B: To avoid paying taxes on research grants
options.C: To make the paper shorter and easier to read
options.D: To ensure readers interpret findings with appropriate caution

explanation: You nailed it! Total honesty about what a study *couldn't* do stops clinicians from misapplying the results on the wards.

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

options.A: To keep the operating room temperature from rising too high
options.B: To ensure the surgeon can see the blood vessels more clearly
options.C: To remove toxic smoke plumes and viral particles from the air
options.D: To prevent the fire alarm system from going off in the hospital

explanation: Electrical surgical tools create smoke containing harmful chemicals and tiny biological particles that theatre staff shouldn't breathe in.

question: A clinic audit reveals low uptake of post-abortion contraception among discharged PAC patients. What is the best quality improvement response for the nursing team?

options.A: Discharge patients immediately without discussing family planning options
options.B: Stop offering all abortion complication treatments until rates improve
options.C: Blame patients for failing to request birth control during their emergency
options.D: Review and strengthen same-day contraceptive counseling and supply availability

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting this gap lets the team fix counseling issues and make sure supplies are ready before discharge.

question: Which of the following is a major financial challenge of using high-fidelity simulation?

options.A: Insurance companies charge high fees for training mannequins
options.B: Mannequins require expensive daily food and water supplies
options.C: High equipment purchase, maintenance, and facility costs
options.D: Students refuse to pay extra fees to use the simulation lab

explanation: Advanced simulators and specialized lab spaces require substantial funding to buy and keep operational. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h7)

question: What should nurses do regarding swab counts during an emergency surgery?

options.A: Perform standard counts with heightened vigilance
options.B: Only count the lap sponges and ignore gauze
options.C: Skip the counts entirely to save precious time
options.D: Let the surgeon count the swabs alone

explanation: Emergencies are intense, but safety rules still apply! We stay extra alert during rushed situations to avoid mistakes.

question: What is the big advantage of running a small pilot study first?

options.A: It helps identify design flaws before a large-scale trial
options.B: It guarantees that the main study will cost no money
options.C: It proves the research hypothesis is 100 percent true
options.D: It replaces the need for an institutional review board

explanation: Spot on! A pilot study is like a dress rehearsal; it lets us fix mistakes before spending big money on the main event.

question: Why must nurses gently correct unverified medication myths with pregnant patients?

options.A: Fear of medication often leads patients to stop vital treatments for chronic illnesses
options.B: Myths alter the pharmacokinetic absorption rate of oral vitamins
options.C: Misinformation causes the placenta to immediately reject all chemical agents
options.D: Patients will otherwise report the nurse to regulatory boards

explanation: When patients are scared by bad info, they might stop taking life-saving medicines. Clear, warm teaching keeps both mom and baby healthy!

question: Which temporary foetal structure turns into the ligamentum arteriosum after birth?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Ductus arteriosus
options.D: Foramen ovale

explanation: Spot on! Once the ductus arteriosus finishes its job and seals up with high oxygen levels, it turns into a sturdy little ligament called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: Why must a patient wait nearly three months to check if lifestyle changes improved his sperm count?

options.A: It takes roughly two to three months for new sperm to fully develop and mature
options.B: Hormone medications prescribed by the doctor require ninety days to activate
options.C: The laboratory needs multiple samples collected over a twelve-week period
options.D: Sperm cells live inside the male reproductive tract for a maximum of ninety days

explanation: Since spermatogenesis takes about 64 to 74 days, any healthy lifestyle changes will take that long to show up in a fresh batch of mature sperm!

question: Why must patients with repaired heart defects take antibiotics before certain dental procedures?

options.A: To prevent infective endocarditis from bacteria entering the bloodstream
options.B: To lower their systemic blood pressure during the dental work
options.C: To keep their surgical chest incision from becoming dry
options.D: To prevent future heart rhythm changes after dental cleaning

explanation: Dental work can release bacteria into the blood. If it lands on repaired heart tissue, it can cause a serious infection called endocarditis. A dose of antibiotics keeps them safe!

question: What is the emergency procedure where a tiny cut is made in the neck membrane to open a blocked airway?

options.A: Removing a tracheostomy tube
options.B: Bronchoscopy
options.C: Cricothyroidotomy
options.D: Thoracentesis

explanation: A cricothyroidotomy is an emergency lifesaving move. When nothing else works and the upper airway is fully shut, healthcare providers cut through the cricothyroid membrane to create a direct path for air.

question: A post-surgical patient cannot pass urine and you suspect they are retaining urine. What is the best bedside tool to check?

options.A: A leg blood flow Doppler
options.B: A portable bladder ultrasound scanner
options.C: A standard chest X-ray
options.D: A full abdominal CT scan

explanation: A portable bladder scanner is quick, non-invasive, and tells you right away how much urine is trapped in the bladder.

question: Why should nurses recommend locally available, affordable foods during nutritional counseling?

options.A: Local foods completely replace the need for drugs
options.B: Expensive imported foods have zero nutrients
options.C: Patients refuse to eat anything foreign
options.D: It ensures the dietary advice is realistic and sustainable

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing advice must fit the patient's real life and pocket so they can actually follow it.

question: A mother living with HIV misses her baby's 6-week immunization and PCR appointment. What is the best community nursing intervention?

options.A: Dispatch a community health worker to trace and counsel the mother gently.
options.B: Remove the infant from the home to ensure proper medication compliance.
options.C: Report the mother immediately to local law enforcement authorities.
options.D: Wait until the mother returns on her own for the one-year checkup.

explanation: Tracing defaulters through community outreach helps find out why they missed appointments and brings them back into care without judgment. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h8)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding drug distribution?

options.A: Calculating the exact molecular weight of every pill
options.B: Surgically placing IV lines directly into brain tissue
options.C: Synthesizing new chemical formulas in the ward
options.D: Monitoring for unexpected side effects from altered drug binding or blood flow

explanation: As a nurse, you are the safety net! Watching how your patient responds and checking their labs helps you catch any drug distribution issues early on.

question: What important safety advice should a nurse give a patient about stopping anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Stop taking them right away if your mouth feels dry
options.B: Reduce the dose slowly as advised by your doctor
options.C: Crush all the tablets so they clear your system faster
options.D: Double the dose if your tremors start coming back

explanation: You've got it! Stopping these meds suddenly can cause rebound muscle stiffness and make tremors flare up fiercely. Always taper safely!

question: What is a very common result of high humidity inside an oxygen tent?

options.A: Water condensation building up on the inner plastic walls
options.B: Sudden dropping of the room's overall humidity level
options.C: Freezing of the oxygen gas into solid ice crystals
options.D: Complete drying out of the patient's nasal passages

explanation: All that moisture in the enclosed space naturally turns into water droplets on the cooler plastic walls of the tent.

question: Which vaccines should nurses recommend to help protect patients against viral STIs and related long-term complications?

options.A: Tetanus and diphtheria
options.B: BCG and yellow fever
options.C: HPV and Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria and typhoid

explanation: Spot on! HPV and Hep B vaccines are powerful shields against major viral infections that can cause serious long-term issues like liver damage or cancers.

question: Why is it risky for a patient to ignore digestive warning signs like bleeding?

options.A: It permanently damages the teeth due to upward pressure from the gut.
options.B: It can delay the diagnosis of serious conditions like bowel obstruction or disease.
options.C: It will automatically cause the patient to develop severe food allergies.
options.D: It stops the liver from producing essential clotting factors.

explanation: Catching serious issues early is key. Ignoring red flags can mean waiting too long to treat a serious gut problem.

question: Why is bone weakened enough to cause a pathological fracture in a patient with chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: The infection turns all the solid bone into liquid fat deposits
options.B: Antibiotic medications dissolve the calcium inside the bone matrix
options.C: Muscles pull so hard on the bone that they snap it in half
options.D: Extensive areas of bone death and destruction compromise the structural integrity

explanation: Areas of necrotic bone and chronic destruction weaken the overall structural framework of the bone, making it prone to breaking under normal stress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: What makes the foramen ovale snap shut at birth?

options.A: Higher pressure in the left atrium compared to the right atrium
options.B: The physical tie placed on the umbilical cord
options.C: Contraction of the heart muscle due to cold air
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's core body temperature

explanation: As blood floods back from the newly working lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure pushes the little flap of the foramen ovale shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: What are the two main categories of hormone disorders?

options.A: Benign or malignant
options.B: Neural or humoral
options.C: Acute or chronic
options.D: Excess or deficiency

explanation: Keep it simple: hormone problems usually happen because the body makes either too much (excess) or too little (deficiency) of a hormone.

question: Why must you always teach patients never to stop taking their antipsychotic medications abruptly on their own?

options.A: It permanently ruins the patient's long-term memory
options.B: Sudden cessation can trigger symptom relapse or withdrawal
options.C: The medication will turn toxic inside the stomach
options.D: It immediately causes permanent kidney failure

explanation: Stopping antipsychotics suddenly can shock the brain chemistry, causing psychotic symptoms to roar right back or triggering uncomfortable withdrawal effects.

question: What should a nurse watch closest right after a patient gets an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Urine output using a bedside commode
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal softness
options.C: Cardiac rhythm and vital signs
options.D: Range of motion in the upper arms

explanation: You've got this! Because the heart muscle was just punctured, tracking heart rhythm and blood pressure helps catch dangerous complications right away.

question: Where can healthcare workers quickly find safety details, hazard warnings, and emergency steps for a specific chemical?

options.A: Hospital dietary meal manual
options.B: Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
options.C: General nursing care textbook
options.D: Daily facility staffing schedule

explanation: Every hospital department has them. The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is your best friend for looking up how to safely handle a chemical and what to do if an accident happens.

question: What is the main goal of surgery when treating a patient with a torn heart muscle?

options.A: Replacing the damaged heart with an artificial mechanical pump
options.B: Directly suturing the tear and relieving pressure in the pericardium
options.C: Removing the entire outer layer of the pericardial sac permanently
options.D: Tying off the coronary arteries to prevent further blood loss

explanation: The surgeon's priority is to stitch up the heart muscle tear and open the sac to drain trapped blood so the heart can beat freely again.

question: Which of these actions should a nurse NOT take when dealing with unhelpful illness behaviour?

options.A: Listen actively to the patient's underlying fears
options.B: Argue aggressively to prove the patient is completely wrong
options.C: Involve medical social workers for holistic support
options.D: Provide clear and simple education about warning signs

explanation: Arguing never works in nursing! It breaks trust and spikes anxiety. We guide with empathy and gentle education instead.

question: What is a key nursing check before giving medication to a pregnant patient?

options.A: Obtain written consent from the hospital pharmacist
options.B: Perform a complete surgical review of systems
options.C: Verify gestational age and assess fetal heart rate
options.D: Prescribe an alternative drug with fewer side effects

explanation: Always check how far along she is and how the baby is doing first, to make sure the drug is safe for that specific stage of pregnancy.

question: Why must sublingual nitroglycerin tablets be stored in a special dark, airtight glass bottle?

options.A: Glass containers prevent the pills from melting in warm weather.
options.B: Light turns the medication into a dangerous poison.
options.C: The medication loses potency easily when exposed to light and air.
options.D: Dark bottles keep the tablets from sticking together.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin loses its strength quickly if light and air get to it, so the special bottle keeps it potent.

question: What is a major plus of using the intraperitoneal route instead of pills for belly issues?

options.A: It completely avoids the need for any sterile equipment or supplies
options.B: It allows patients to self-administer complex chemotherapy at home
options.C: It delivers higher local drug concentrations directly to the target area
options.D: It eliminates all risks of systemic side effects and infection

explanation: Brilliant! Going straight to the source means the medication hits the problem area hard and fast, way better than waiting for a pill to digest. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which ethical principle gives a competent patient the right to refuse a prescribed medication?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy is all about respecting the patient's right to make independent choices about their own body and healthcare journey.

question: A patient is brought to the clinic after a motorcycle crash, and clear fluid is dripping from one nostril. What serious injury should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Severe allergic reaction to helmet padding
options.B: Fracture of the cribriform plate with CSF leak
options.C: Rupture of the maxillary paranasal sinus
options.D: Inflammation of Kiesselbach's vascular plexus

explanation: Clear fluid coming from the nose after a head impact is a major red flag. It usually means a skull fracture has torn the lining near the brain, letting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak out. Always report this immediately!

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to chart after giving a rectal medication?

options.A: Any local discomfort or side effects noted
options.B: The patient's favorite hobby or pastime
options.C: The exact time and date of administration
options.D: The specific name and dose of the drug

explanation: Personal hobbies have nothing to do with clinical charting. Always focus on the drug name, dose, time, and patient response!

question: What major organ side effect must nurses watch out for when patients take drugs like isoniazid and rifampicin?

options.A: Liver toxicity or hepatotoxicity
options.B: Sudden bone fractures
options.C: Permanent kidney failure
options.D: Complete hair loss

explanation: First-line TB drugs are processed by the liver, so nurses must monitor closely for signs of liver stress or toxicity.

question: How does untreated cervicitis affect a patient's risk of contracting HIV?

options.A: It grants temporary immunity against sexually transmitted viruses.
options.B: It decreases the risk because white blood cells destroy the virus.
options.C: It increases the risk because the mucosal tissue is broken and immune cells are rushed to the area.
options.D: It has no measurable impact on viral transmission rates.

explanation: Inflamed, fragile tissue plus a gathering of immune cells gives viruses like HIV an easier pathway into the body.

question: Why does relaxing the muscle around the airways make breathing easier?

options.A: It increases airway radius and lowers resistance to airflow
options.B: It stops the lungs from producing excess fluid
options.C: It completely cures chronic lung inflammation
options.D: It strengthens the diaphragm muscle during inhalation

explanation: Think of a garden hose: when you relax a tight squeeze, the pipe opens up and water flows smoothly. It's the same idea for air flowing into the lungs!

question: What medical term describes a constant ringing or buzzing sound in the ears?

options.A: Vertigo
options.B: Tinnitus
options.C: Otitis
options.D: Presbycusis

explanation: Tinnitus is a very common issue where a person hears phantom sounds like ringing or buzzing when no external sound is actually there.

question: Which of these situations calls for immediate surgery in genitourinary trauma?

options.A: Hemodynamic instability and active internal bleeding
options.B: A small bruise on the skin over the lower ribs
options.C: Mild hematuria that clears up within two hours
options.D: Anxiety about the hospital environment

explanation: If a patient's vital signs are crashing because of ongoing internal bleeding, surgery is needed right away to stop the leak. Safety first!

question: A patient with type 1 diabetes lives somewhere without reliable electricity and asks how to keep their insulin cool. What is a helpful, practical suggestion?

options.A: Use a clay pot evaporative cooler system to store the insulin safely
options.B: Keep the insulin bottle in direct sunlight to keep it warm and dry
options.C: Store the insulin inside the family cooking pot near the fireplace
options.D: Leave the insulin exposed on the open windowsill during the night

explanation: Brilliant! A clay pot cooler (pot-in-pot evaporative cooling) is a fantastic, traditional way to lower storage temperatures without needing a fridge or electricity.

question: Which of the following is a major barrier to safe motherhood in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of fully equipped emergency hospitals
options.B: Too many skilled midwives working in remote villages
options.C: Free transportation services for all pregnant women
options.D: Inadequate health infrastructure and out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Poor facilities and the burden of paying out-of-pocket for treatment prevent many Nigerian women from getting timely care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: A patient complains of mild tummy upset every time they take their naproxen. What is a great first piece of advice?

options.A: Crush the tablet and mix it into citrus juice
options.B: Stop taking the medication immediately forever
options.C: Double the dose to get used to the drug faster
options.D: Take the medication with food or milk

explanation: Food or a glass of milk acts like a gentle cushion for the stomach lining, shielding it from direct irritation. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why is 'replication' (repeating a study) so important in scientific nursing research?

options.A: It proves that the researcher is more important than the clinician
options.B: It helps verify whether original results were accurate and reliable
options.C: It eliminates the need for patient consent in clinical trials
options.D: It ensures that hospital policies never change again

explanation: When different researchers repeat a study and get the same results, we can trust that the findings are solid and dependable.

question: What is the best way to handle a patient who is extremely anxious about minor symptoms?

options.A: Scold them for wasting valuable hospital time
options.B: Discharge them immediately from the clinic ward
options.C: Validate their feelings and offer gentle reassurance
options.D: Ignore their complaints until lab results come out

explanation: Never dismiss their fear! Validating their emotions builds instant trust and helps them calm down.

question: What is the primary feature that helps distinguish fat embolism syndrome from other post-fracture complications?

options.A: High fever and visible pus draining from a wound
options.B: Complete lack of pain at the site of the broken bone
options.C: Respiratory distress combined with a petechial skin rash
options.D: Slow bone healing over a period of several years

explanation: Fat globules traveling to the lungs and skin typically cause breathing difficulties paired with a characteristic pinpoint red rash. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h9)

question: What is the main purpose of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish patients who failed to report their symptoms early
options.B: To test new antibiotics on healthy community members
options.C: To disinfect all public water systems in the region
options.D: To identify individuals who may have been exposed to an infection source

explanation: Contact tracing is like detective work—we track down everyone who crossed paths with an infected person so we can protect and monitor them early.

question: How do most medications pass from a nursing mother's blood into her breast milk?

options.A: Cellular phagocytosis
options.B: Active transport pumps
options.C: Passive diffusion
options.D: Direct ductal injection

explanation: Just like with the placenta, drugs usually drift naturally across membranes into breast milk based on concentration and fat solubility.

question: A patient has signs of hormone overproduction because their feedback loop broke. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Blood metabolite levels have successfully stabilized all endocrine organs
options.B: The target gland or pituitary fails to respond to negative feedback inhibition
options.C: The hypothalamus stops releasing releasing factors entirely and permanently
options.D: Neural stimulation of the adrenal medulla has permanently shut down

explanation: If the 'off switch' (negative feedback) stops working, the gland keeps pumping out hormones without stopping, leading to overproduction.

question: What is the typical clinical effect of a beta-blocker drug?

options.A: Stimulation of digestive motility and saliva production
options.B: Decreased heart rate and lowered blood pressure
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels and pupils
options.D: Increased heart rate and dilated bronchial tubes

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline from working on the heart, helping it beat slower and with less force. This is great for managing high blood pressure!

question: When is the best time to document a rectal suppository in the patient's records?

options.A: Immediately after the procedure is completed
options.B: Before gathering the supplies from the cart
options.C: At the end of the entire nursing shift
options.D: Only if the patient complains of pain later

explanation: Charting right away keeps your records accurate and prevents medication errors. Great job keeping up with your duties!

question: Which of these is NOT part of a routine check on a new mother's digestive recovery?

options.A: Asking when she last opened her bowels
options.B: Checking for bowel sounds and passage of gas
options.C: Assessing perineal discomfort during elimination
options.D: Inspecting the abdomen for signs of surgical wound breakdown

explanation: While surgical wound checks are vital after a C-section, general bowel recovery is all about checking for gas, bowel movements, and comfort down below.

question: What is the most important advice a nurse should give a patient taking a multi-week course of antifungal drugs?

options.A: Double the next dose whenever a single daily dose is accidentally missed
options.B: Take the pills only on days when itching or burning becomes severe
options.C: Complete the entire prescribed course even if symptoms disappear early
options.D: Stop the medication immediately if mild skin dryness or nausea occurs

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping early is the number one reason fungal infections bounce right back. Always encourage patients to finish the full dose.

question: A patient has muffled heart sounds and a sudden blood pressure crash after an intracardiac injection. What is happening?

options.A: Normal recovery
options.B: A urinary tract infection
options.C: Cardiac tamponade
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Spot on! Blood pooling inside the sac around the heart dampens the heart sounds and stops the heart from filling with blood, crashing the blood pressure.

question: What is a common complication directly caused by skin traction straps and boots?

options.A: Permanent overgrowth of bone callus
options.B: Total loss of joint flexibility forever
options.C: Skin breakdown and pressure ulcer formation
options.D: Severe infection inside the bone marrow

explanation: Constant pressure from boots and tapes can easily irritate the skin. That's why regular skin checks are a nurse's best friend!

question: Which detail is essential to record for tracking vaccine safety and batches?

options.A: The brand of syringe plunger
options.B: Clinic room temperature
options.C: Batch and lot number
options.D: The client's favorite hobby

explanation: Lot and batch numbers connect every vaccine dose back to the factory, helping health authorities trace products if safety checks are ever needed.

question: What medical term describes when a gland makes too little hormone?

options.A: Pulsatile rhythm
options.B: Hyposecretion
options.C: Humoral stimulus
options.D: Hypersecretion

explanation: 'Hypo-' means under or low, so hyposecretion simply means the gland is producing less hormone than the body needs.

question: Which sign tells you a mixed lotion should be thrown away immediately?

options.A: A label showing it was mixed three days ago
options.B: Visible separation or discoloration
options.C: A smooth and uniform texture throughout
options.D: A slight cooling sensation upon skin contact

explanation: If the cream separates or changes color, it means it has gone bad and is no longer safe to use. You're doing great!

question: Why is a Pap smear so important when you spot a red patch on the cervix?

options.A: To chemically destroy the extra columnar cells on the surface
options.B: To measure the exact hormonal levels circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: To rule out malignant or pre-cancerous changes that can look similar to benign erosion
options.D: To prove that the patient has an active bacterial infection

explanation: Harmless ectropion can sometimes look very similar to early cellular changes or cancer. A Pap smear helps us be 100% sure the patient is safe.

question: Why should you always look closely at the tip of the nasogastric tube right after removing it?

options.A: To measure the patient's stomach length
options.B: To check how much stomach acid is left on it
options.C: To make sure the whole tube came out in one piece and nothing broke off inside
options.D: To check if the patient chewed on the plastic

explanation: Checking the removed tube ensures no broken bits were left behind in the patient's stomach or food pipe. A quick glance saves a lot of trouble!

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent leaving items inside a patient?

options.A: Rushing through the final count to finish quickly
options.B: Using standardized hospital safety checklists
options.C: Minimizing operating room noise during counts
options.D: Encouraging open communication among staff

explanation: Never rush a count! Taking your time, staying calm, and keeping the room quiet helps catch errors.

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding advance directives upon patient admission?

options.A: Deciding whether the living will is legally valid without a doctor
options.B: Writing the legal documents for the patient using hospital letterhead
options.C: Notifying the local court system that a new patient has arrived
options.D: Asking about existing directives and placing copies in the medical record

explanation: Nurses routinely screen for advance directives upon admission to ensure the care team knows the patient's preferences from the start. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: An IV bag of 1,000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a pump. What is the hourly rate?

options.A: 150 mL/hr
options.B: 80 mL/hr
options.C: 125 mL/hr
options.D: 100 mL/hr

explanation: Divide total volume by total hours: 1,000 mL ÷ 8 hours = 125 mL/hr.

question: A nurse teaches villagers to boil their drinking water to stop cholera. Which part of the disease chain is this targeting?

options.A: The genetic makeup of the host
options.B: The incubation period of the germ
options.C: The vehicle of transmission
options.D: The virulence of the pathogen

explanation: Water acts as the 'vehicle' carrying the germ to people. Boiling it breaks the chain right there. Brilliant public health nursing!

question: What is a common reason why vaccines accidentally freeze inside a health clinic fridge?

options.A: Setting the refrigerator temperature above plus 10 degrees Celsius
options.B: Using digital data loggers instead of paper logs
options.C: Keeping facility doors locked during weekends
options.D: Placing sensitive vaccines too close to the freezer compartment

explanation: Be careful where you place stock! The parts right next to the freezer section can easily drop below zero and ruin freeze-sensitive doses.

question: What is the big danger if you fail to mix a diluted lotion thoroughly?

options.A: Extending the expiration date by several months
options.B: Turning the entire mixture into a watery liquid
options.C: Creating concentrated hot spots that irritate the skin
options.D: Changing the color of the cream to bright yellow

explanation: If you don't mix it well, pockets of high-strength medicine can hide in the cream and sting the patient's skin.

question: If a community has high rates of illiteracy, how should nurses adjust their health education strategy?

options.A: Only people who went to secondary school are allowed to visit the clinic
options.B: Nurses must rely more on verbal talks, drama, and pictures than written pamphlets
options.C: Written textbooks become the primary method of teaching villagers
options.D: Health education must be completely cancelled until everyone learns to read

explanation: When people cannot read written text easily, visual aids, storytelling, local drama, and spoken words are wonderful ways to get the health message across! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)

question: A nursing student in a sterile gown accidentally lets their hands drop below their waist. What should they do?

options.A: Step back one foot and continue assisting the surgeon
options.B: Continue working because the gown is still clean on top
options.C: Acknowledge that sterility is broken and get a new gown
options.D: Ask the circulating nurse to wipe the gloves with alcohol

explanation: In theatre rules, anything below the waist is considered unsterile. Don't worry—accidents happen! Just step back, re-gown, and keep learning.

question: What advice should a nurse give to help a patient maintain healthy vaginal flora?

options.A: Use scented soaps daily inside the vaginal canal for deep cleaning.
options.B: Wear tight synthetic underwear to keep the area dry.
options.C: Avoid harsh vaginal douches that disrupt protective bacteria.
options.D: Stop taking prescribed antibiotics as soon as itching stops.

explanation: Fantastic! Douching washes away the good bacteria (lactobacilli) and messes with natural pH, making it way easier for bad germs and yeast to take over.

question: What is the main job of luteinizing hormone (LH) in the male body?

options.A: To stimulate testosterone production
options.B: To help mature sperm in the epididymis
options.C: To relax the muscles of the urethra
options.D: To produce the fluid in seminal vesicles

explanation: LH travels through the bloodstream and targets the Leydig cells in the testes, giving them the green light to make testosterone.

question: Which of these details must you include when charting steam tent therapy?

options.A: The brand name of the plastic tent canopy
options.B: The exact electrical voltage of the wall socket
options.C: The name of the manufacturer who built the bed
options.D: Start and end times of the treatment

explanation: You got it! Accurate start and end times give a clear timeline of the care you provided.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop in the human body?

options.A: Parathyroid hormone halting when blood calcium levels normalize
options.B: Insulin stopping the release of glucose once blood sugar drops
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH release when levels are high

explanation: Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback amplifies a signal! During labor, oxytocin makes contractions stronger, which releases even *more* oxytocin until the baby is born.

question: Which part of the brain kicks off the reproductive hormone cycle by releasing GnRH?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Testis
options.C: Pituitary gland
options.D: Prostate gland

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master control center in the brain. It secretes GnRH to wake up the pituitary gland and start the hormone chain reaction.

question: What minimum level of medication adherence is needed to keep HIV fully suppressed over the long term?

options.A: Around 50%
options.B: Exactly 20%
options.C: At least 95%
options.D: Only on weekends

explanation: You got it! HIV treatment requires consistency. Taking at least 95% of doses on schedule keeps the virus cornered and unable to fight back.

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: What is the biggest perk of using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in emergency or acute care?

options.A: It gives instant answers right at the bedside to guide fast care
options.B: It requires no training for hospital staff to use
options.C: It replaces every single blood test in the emergency room
options.D: It offers higher picture quality than giant hospital machines

explanation: POCUS is designed to be quick and portable, giving clinicians immediate answers right when every second counts.

question: What standard assessment tool do nurses use to monitor patients for early signs of tardive dyskinesia?

options.A: APGAR scoring system
options.B: Braden Scale for Pressure Ulcers
options.C: AIMS (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale)
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: We use the AIMS scale during regular check-ups to score any involuntary twitching or movements so we catch tardive dyskinesia early.

question: What is a key nursing responsibility when using continuous pulse oximetry on a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Leaving the same sensor taped to one finger for the entire week
options.B: Relying solely on the digital number without looking at the patient
options.C: Moving the sensor to a new site periodically to prevent skin breakdown
options.D: Turning off the audible alarm so patients can sleep peacefully

explanation: Continuous pressure from a sensor probe can damage fragile skin, so nurses must rotate the monitoring site regularly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of meningitis?

options.A: High fever and body chills
options.B: Sudden complete paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe and pounding headache
options.D: Stiff and painful neck movement

explanation: Spot on! Meningitis causes terrible headaches, fever, and a stiff neck, but leg paralysis is not a standard sign of the infection.

question: Why does a lack of dystrophin cause muscle damage in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?

options.A: The muscle cell membrane becomes fragile and tears during normal contractions.
options.B: The muscle cells lose their ability to receive nerve impulses from the spinal cord.
options.C: Satellite cells multiply too quickly and crowd out functional muscle tissue.
options.D: Calcium builds up in the cell and immediately dissolves the bones.

explanation: Without dystrophin to absorb the shock, the outer membrane of the muscle cell easily tears every time the muscle contracts. You're building solid clinical knowledge!

question: Why do freshly mixed (reconstituted) suspensions expire much faster than dry powders?

options.A: The active drug evaporates into the air inside the room
options.B: The plastic bottle begins to melt in the refrigerator
options.C: Water activates chemical breakdown and microbial growth
options.D: Refrigeration destroys the chemical bonds of the powder

explanation: Water wakes everything up! Once water is added, it triggers chemical breakdown and creates a cozy home for bacteria to multiply. That's why they don't last long.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to health behavior change in primary care?

options.A: High rates of illiteracy among the target audience
options.B: Extreme poverty and lack of basic financial resources
options.C: Deep-seated cultural norms and traditional beliefs
options.D: Guaranteed financial wealth for every household

explanation: Poverty, illiteracy, and strong cultural traditions can make health changes tough, but having guaranteed wealth certainly wouldn't be a barrier! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)

question: In which direction should you smooth a topical lotion onto a patient's skin?

options.A: Strictly from the bottom of the limb upward
options.B: In a crisscross pattern across the rash
options.C: In the direction of hair growth
options.D: In tight circular motions against the hair

explanation: Smoothing lotions in the direction of hair growth keeps hair follicles happy and prevents painful inflammation.

question: A nurse notices a patient's pulse oximeter reading drop suddenly from 98% to 82% while the patient is sleeping peacefully and breathing easily. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check the sensor position and ensure the patient has not slipped it off
options.B: Immediately start emergency mouth-to-mouth resuscitation
options.C: Call the doctor to declare a cardiac arrest code
options.D: Administer a stat dose of intravenous adrenaline

explanation: Sudden unrealistic drops without physical signs of distress usually point to a displaced sensor, loose cable, or motion artifact. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h8)

question: What do we call the solid, mulberry-like cluster of cells formed during early embryonic travel?

options.A: Pronucleus
options.B: Zygote
options.C: Morula
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: Spot on! The morula is a solid little cluster of cells that looks a bit like a tiny mulberry as it travels down the tube.

question: What is the medical term for an infection and inflammation of the meninges?

options.A: Meningitis
options.B: Hematoma
options.C: Neuritis
options.D: Encephalitis

explanation: Easy peasy! Whenever you see '-itis' at the end of a medical word, it means inflammation. So, inflammation of the meninges is meningitis.

question: Which eye condition is an absolute contraindication for anticholinergic medications?

options.A: Conjunctivitis
options.B: Cataracts
options.C: Color blindness
options.D: Glaucoma

explanation: Anticholinergics dilate the pupil, which can trap fluid inside the eye and dangerously worsen glaucoma. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is the biggest downside or risk linked to the intraperitoneal route?

options.A: High risk of infection and peritonitis
options.B: Complete failure of the human respiratory system
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Instantaneous destruction of all oral medications

explanation: You got it! Anytime you open up or access the sterile peritoneal cavity, germs can sneak in, making infection and peritonitis the main danger to watch for. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h7)

question: What does 'drop factor' mean when setting up a gravity IV line?

options.A: How fast blood pressure drops
options.B: The number of drops in one milliliter for that specific tubing set
options.C: The maximum speed for potassium
options.D: The total time for an IV bag to empty

explanation: Check the IV tubing box! The drop factor tells you how many drops (gtt) make up 1 mL, like 15 gtt/mL.

question: What should a nurse do FIRST immediately after discovering a medication error has occurred?

options.A: Call the hospital security department to investigate
options.B: Hide the incident report form so nobody finds out
options.C: Leave the ward immediately to avoid disciplinary action
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide necessary care

explanation: Patient safety and immediate clinical evaluation always take priority over paperwork or administrative reporting when an error happens. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: A patient is prescribed a new synergistic drug combo. What is a key nursing duty before giving it?

options.A: Restricting the patient from drinking any water for 24 hours
options.B: Telling the patient they can double the dose if pain increases
options.C: Checking baseline organ function tests and verify correct dosing
options.D: Stopping all other routine medications without physician approval

explanation: As a sharp nurse, you always check baseline labs like kidney and liver function first to make sure the patient can safely handle the combination.

question: What should you check first if the oxygen level inside the tent suddenly goes down?

options.A: The hospital's central pharmacy inventory
options.B: The expiration date of the plastic canopy
options.C: Tubing connections and canopy edge seals
options.D: The patient's blood pressure and heart rate

explanation: Always check your basics first! Loose tubing or edges that popped out from under the mattress are usually why oxygen is leaking out.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe or recommended way to lower your risk of getting an STI?

options.A: Receiving available prophylactic vaccinations against viral pathogens
options.B: Using barrier methods like condoms consistently and correctly
options.C: Relying solely on herbal supplements to block infection transmission
options.D: Undergoing routine periodic STI screenings with new or multiple partners

explanation: Herbal mixtures won't stop an STI! Safe practices mean using condoms, getting vaccinated, and going for regular checks.

question: What happens to joint structures over many years if metabolic joint disease is left completely untreated?

options.A: Complete regeneration of healthy joint tissue and natural healing
options.B: Softening of the bones until they become completely flexible
options.C: Permanent bone erosion, cartilage destruction, and severe deformity
options.D: Total fusion of the skin directly to the underlying muscle tissue

explanation: Without treatment, ongoing inflammation and tophi will gradually wear down the bone and cartilage, leading to permanent joint damage.

question: Why must standing order protocols be reviewed and updated regularly?

options.A: Older protocols automatically expire and turn invisible after thirty days
options.B: Medical guidelines and disease treatment recommendations change over time
options.C: Government printing presses need new contracts every single month
options.D: Patients prefer reading newly printed paper booklets during visits

explanation: Clinical practice evolves as new evidence emerges, so standing orders must be updated to reflect current, safe medical standards. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h9)

question: What is the main danger of leaving clear units of measurement off a bar chart's axis?

options.A: The hospital will fail to meet basic fire safety codes
options.B: The chart software will crash and delete the saved file
options.C: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed medications
options.D: Readers may misinterpret the data and make poor clinical decisions

explanation: Without clear units, nobody can tell if the numbers represent counts, percentages, or money. Always label your axes!

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to ensure a patient can safely manage complex wound care and dressing changes at home?

options.A: Tell the patient to wait until the wound heals entirely on its own
options.B: Assume the family knows what to do because dressing changes are simple
options.C: Ask the patient to read a medical textbook chapter before leaving the hospital
options.D: Provide written instructions and have the patient demonstrate the technique back

explanation: Return demonstration combined with written instructions ensures the patient or caregiver actually understands and can perform the steps correctly at home. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h8)

question: Which of the following is a frequent long-term complication of poorly treated acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

explanation: When acute bone infections are not fully eradicated, they frequently transition into long-standing chronic osteomyelitis with recurrent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: A patient is given a minor tranquilizer for short-term stress. What key safety advice should you give them before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how the drug affects you
options.B: Mix the medication with a glass of wine to help it absorb faster
options.C: Stop taking the pills abruptly whenever you feel better
options.D: Double the dose if your stress level doubles during the day

explanation: Because these drugs cause drowsiness and slow down reflexes, patients need to steer clear of hazardous tasks until they see how their body reacts.

question: How does naloxone work to reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: By speeding up renal excretion of the drug through urination
options.B: By binding directly to the free poison molecules in the stomach
options.C: By competing for and blocking opioid receptor sites
options.D: By stimulating the liver to break down the circulating toxin

explanation: Naloxone acts like a key that bumps the opioid off its lock (the receptor). By blocking those sites, it quickly wakes the patient up and helps them breathe again.

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting periodic chart audits in a primary health clinic?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours required for staff
options.B: To increase the cost of consultation fees for incoming patients
options.C: To check if staff are following standing order protocols correctly
options.D: To punish nurses who make spelling mistakes in their writing

explanation: Chart audits help supervisors evaluate clinical practice, ensure protocol adherence, and identify areas needing further training. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h9)

question: Which rare, serious skin and tissue condition can develop in patients with bad kidney function who receive gadolinium contrast?

options.A: Acute radiation sickness
options.B: Chronic bone marrow failure
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
options.D: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

explanation: Well done! Gadolinium can trigger this serious condition in patients whose kidneys are struggling to filter waste.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Use barrier methods consistently to help prevent reinfection.
options.B: Make sure your sexual partner is treated at the same time.
options.C: Stop taking your medicine as soon as the discharge lessens.
options.D: Avoid having sex until your treatment is fully completed.

explanation: Never advise stopping meds early just because symptoms fade. They must finish the entire course!

question: Which of the following describes an independent double-check for high-risk medication calculations?

options.A: The doctor and patient calculate the pill count together at discharge
options.B: The pharmacist calculates the dose and the nurse administers it without review
options.C: One nurse calculates the dose twice on two different patient charts
options.D: Two nurses calculate the dose separately without discussing their numbers beforehand

explanation: Independent double-checks require two clinicians to work out the math separately to catch hidden errors before administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h9)

question: Why are primary health care nurses usually the ones doing community counselling?

options.A: They are often the first point of contact for community members
options.B: They have legal authority to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.C: They have specialized degrees in clinical psychology
options.D: They spend most of their time in large urban hospitals

explanation: Because primary care nurses work right in the community, people naturally trust them and turn to them first for help.

question: What is the most important thing a nurse should do when abnormal moulding shows up on the partograph?

options.A: Document the finding and wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.B: Report the finding promptly to the doctor or senior midwife
options.C: Perform an operative vaginal delivery without waiting for assistance
options.D: Restrict all oral fluids to prevent further swelling of the head

explanation: Never keep dangerous findings to yourself! Speak up and report worsening signs like severe moulding right away so the team can jump into action.

question: Where should used injection needles be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: A red biohazard bag for soft waste
options.B: A standard black plastic trash bag
options.C: A rigid, puncture-proof sharps container
options.D: The side pocket of the nurse's uniform

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries for nurses and housekeeping staff. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: What should you do right away if the tent's cooling motor stops working during your shift?

options.A: Notify maintenance, monitor temperature closely, and provide temporary ventilation
options.B: Wrap the child in extra heavy blankets to prevent shivering
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow rate to maximum to cool the air down
options.D: Disconnect the oxygen entirely and move the child to a regular chair

explanation: A broken cooler will cause heat to build up inside. Call maintenance right away, keep an eye on the temperature, and fan or ventilate carefully to keep the child safe.

question: What is a major, life-threatening complication that can happen if bone infections are left untreated?

options.A: Permanent vision loss in both eyes
options.B: Total loss of stomach acid
options.C: Sepsis and septic shock
options.D: Sudden development of asthma

explanation: When an infection escapes the bone and enters the bloodstream, it can cause a whole-body emergency known as sepsis. Catching it early is key!

question: What instruction should you give your patient right before you pull out a nasogastric tube?

options.A: Cough gently to clear the throat
options.B: Swallow hard several times
options.C: Blow air out forcefully through the mouth
options.D: Take a deep breath and hold it

explanation: Holding the breath closes the windpipe, keeping the lungs safe from breathing in any leftover fluid as the tube slides out.

question: What is the recommended infant feeding practice for mothers living on ART where replacement feeding is unsafe?

options.A: Exclusive use of herbal teas and plain water
options.B: Immediate weaning onto cow milk on day one
options.C: Strict formula feeding without any breast milk
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best balance of nutrition and protection against HIV transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe safety practice in the operating room?

options.A: Using smoke evacuation systems for electrosurgical units
options.B: Disposing of used scalpel blades in puncture-resistant containers
options.C: Wearing protective eyewear to shield against blood splashes
options.D: Recapping used injection needles by hand before disposal

explanation: Never recap needles with both hands! It is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and is strictly discouraged.

question: What should you do to the skin before putting on a newly diluted medicated lotion?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of oil to seal the pores
options.B: Clean and dry the skin gently
options.C: Scrub the area firmly with an antiseptic pad
options.D: Warm the skin with a heating pad for ten minutes

explanation: A gentle wash removes dirt without upsetting the skin barrier. Nice and easy!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of intraperitoneal administration?

options.A: Catheter blockage
options.B: Peritonitis
options.C: Abdominal pain
options.D: Inhalation pneumonia

explanation: Correct! Inhalation pneumonia is a lung issue, so it's not a direct local complication of accessing the peritoneal belly cavity. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses in Nigeria to ask patients about any traditional herbal remedies they might be taking?

options.A: Traditional herbs are scientifically proven to cure type 1 diabetes permanently
options.B: Herbal products completely replace the need for blood glucose monitoring
options.C: Traditional remedies have no chemical impact on human liver enzymes
options.D: Herbal mixtures can interact with prescribed drugs and cause unexpected blood sugar drops

explanation: Spot on! Many local herbal preparations can unexpectedly drop blood sugar levels, leading to severe hypoglycaemia when mixed with regular diabetes medications.

question: What is the primary reason nurses 'cohort' patients in a hospital ward?

options.A: To make it easier for doctors to prescribe the exact same medication
options.B: To ensure that patients with different diseases share recovery rooms
options.C: To group patients with the same infection together to contain transmission
options.D: To reduce the total number of nursing staff required on the ward

explanation: Cohorting means putting patients with the exact same bug in one designated area so they don't spread it to uninfected patients.

question: In nursing safety terms, what is a 'near-miss'?

options.A: An error that is caught just in time before it reaches the patient
options.B: A minor allergic rash that goes away without medical treatment
options.C: A patient who refuses to take their prescribed medication
options.D: A drug that expired on the shelf and was thrown away safely
