explanation: A near-miss is a lucky catch! It's an error spotted right before it harms the patient, giving the team a great chance to fix the system so it doesn't happen again.

question: What serious condition is strongly suspected when you see severe, locked Grade 3 moulding during labour?

options.A: Normal physiological descent
options.B: Premature rupture of membranes
options.C: Rapid precipitate delivery
options.D: Obstructed labour

explanation: Grade 3 moulding means the bones are tightly locked and won't budge. That's a major red flag telling us the labour is blocked.

question: An adult child is crying and demanding that staff restart all life support for a dying parent, even though the parent has a clear living will stating otherwise. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Act as an advocate for the patient by gently reminding the family of the documented wishes
options.B: Tell the family that their opinion does not matter at all in the hospital
options.C: Immediately follow the child's orders to stop the family conflict
options.D: Call hospital security to remove the family member from the room

explanation: The nurse bridges the gap with compassion, offering emotional support while firmly upholding the documented autonomy of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty right after a patient finishes an MRI where they received mild sedation?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake for the next twelve hours to prevent swelling
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the unit to clear the drugs
options.C: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness until the sedative wears off
options.D: Perform a complete neurological exam every five minutes for two hours

explanation: You got it! Keeping a close eye on vital signs and alertness helps ensure the patient safely recovers from the sedative.

question: Why are proper body positioning and early splinting so important in burn rehab?

options.A: To prevent debilitating joint contractures caused by scar tightening
options.B: To maintain adequate arterial blood pressure in the extremities
options.C: To speed up the re-epithelialization of superficial donor sites
options.D: To stop the hypermetabolic energy expenditure phase early

explanation: Healing burn scars love to pull and tighten joints into awkward bends. Splints and good positioning keep patients stretched out and moving freely!

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.
options.B: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill.
options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger.

question: Besides published research, what else does evidence-based nursing practice bring together?

options.A: Superstition and historical habits
options.B: Personal intuition and strict tradition
options.C: Clinical expertise and patient preferences
options.D: Hospital budgets and physician seniority

explanation: Good evidence-based practice blends the best research with your own clinical judgment and what matters most to the patient.

question: A hospital director in Lagos wants to start primary nursing on a busy surgical ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ensure an adequate mix of registered staff and provide training on clinical autonomy.
options.B: Fire all doctors on the ward to give nurses complete control over the hospital.
options.C: Reduce the number of visiting hours to zero minutes per day.
options.D: Ban patients from asking questions about their medications.

explanation: To make primary nursing work, management must first ensure there are enough qualified nurses and empower them to make independent clinical decisions.

question: Why must you carefully educate a patient about the drug that caused their idiosyncratic reaction?

options.A: To help the patient learn how to manufacture the medicine at home
options.B: To prevent accidental re-exposure to the same dangerous drug in the future
options.C: So the patient can demand financial compensation from the pharmacy
options.D: So the patient can share the leftover pills with family members

explanation: If a patient takes that same drug again later, their body will react even faster and much more severely. Clear patient teaching keeps them safe for life!

question: What device can a patient in lower limb skin traction use to safely lift their body for position changes?

options.A: Overhead trapeze bar
options.B: Padded arm restraints
options.C: Bedside footboard
options.D: Adjustable side rails

explanation: The trapeze bar lets patients use their upper body strength to lift their hips for bedpans or back care without messing up their traction alignment. Brilliant setup!

question: Which of the following is NOT an early sign of respiratory distress or hypoxia?

options.A: Calm and relaxed sleeping behavior
options.B: Increased breathing rate (tachypnea)
options.C: Restlessness and sudden anxiety
options.D: Mild confusion or disorientation

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of left-sided heart failure?

options.A: Enlarged and tender liver
options.B: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.C: Visible bulging of the neck veins
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: When the left side of the heart struggles, blood backs up into the lungs, causing fluid buildup, breathlessness, and lung crackles.

question: What is the main job of the trophoblast layer in a developing blastocyst?

options.A: It surrounds the egg to form the protective corona radiata
options.B: It forms the outer layer that assists with implantation and placenta development
options.C: It develops directly into the internal organs of the growing fetus
options.D: It creates the fast block to prevent extra sperm from entering

question: What key advice should you give a patient with mild COVID-19 who is well enough to stay home?

options.A: Visit crowded public areas to build natural community immunity
options.B: Stop wearing a mask immediately once the fever drops
options.C: Avoid drinking fluids so that coughing spells decrease
options.D: Stay home in isolation to avoid spreading the virus to others

question: What is the main goal of having burn survivors wear custom pressure garments during recovery?

options.A: To prevent the development of deep vein thrombosis
options.B: To protect the fragile skin from ultraviolet sun rays
options.C: To provide continuous warmth to grafted skin areas
options.D: To minimize hypertrophic scarring and flatten keloids

explanation: Constant, gentle pressure helps train healing collagen fibers to lie flat, keeping raised scars and keloids under control over time.

question: Why does the rest of the baby's body slide out so quickly once the shoulders are born?

options.A: Maternal adrenaline production peaks right before delivery

options.C: The amniotic fluid acts as a lubricant for the lower body

question: What kind of drug property makes it most likely to build up in breast milk for the baby to absorb?

options.A: A long half-life combined with high lipid solubility
options.B: High protein binding capacity in maternal blood
options.C: Water solubility with a very long elimination time
options.D: Complete destruction by the maternal stomach acid

explanation: Drugs that dissolve easily in fat (lipid-soluble) and hang around in the body a long time (long half-life) tend to linger in breast milk.

question: Why is it important to write down how the patient tolerated the treatment and how much mucus they cleared?

options.A: It shows how much water the machine used up
options.B: It proves the effectiveness of the treatment
options.C: It determines the hospital room billing costs
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical assessment

explanation: Brilliant! Documenting their response helps the whole healthcare team see that the therapy was successful.

question: Why should nurses teach patients to avoid unprescribed supplements when taking synergistic drugs?

options.A: Additional substances could trigger unpredictable and dangerous interactions
options.B: Supplements always neutralize the healing properties of prescription drugs
options.C: Supplements make laboratory blood draws completely inaccurate
options.D: Over-the-counter products are illegal to take alongside antibiotics

explanation: Over-the-counter herbs and supplements can mess with drug processing in the body, leading to accidental overdoses or weird reactions.

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive imported supplements prescribed elsewhere. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital management
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether
options.C: Tell them to borrow money to buy the brand
options.D: Help the patient find affordable local whole-food alternatives

explanation: Brilliant! As a nurse, you bridge the gap by showing patients how to get great nutrition using what is easily available around them.

question: Why do we follow a step-by-step reporting ladder for injection safety data?

options.A: It allows individual nurses to bypass hospital management
options.B: It prevents state and federal officers from seeing local clinic errors
options.C: It ensures that paperwork stays inside the hospital indefinitely
options.D: It allows data to be properly aggregated for national procurement planning

explanation: Spot on! Gathering data upward gives the country the accurate totals it needs to buy and distribute supplies for everyone.

question: Why must men with an enlarged prostate be very careful with central anticholinergics?

options.A: Prostate tissue destroys the active drug instantly

options.C: The drugs can cause or worsen trouble passing urine

question: During a neuro exam, a patient struggles to quickly flip their hand back and forth to tap their palm. What is this finding called?

options.A: Cerebellar nystagmus
options.B: Expressive aphasia
options.C: Dysdiadochokinesia
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy

question: What crucial detail must you write on a newly mixed (reconstituted) suspension bottle?

options.B: The exact date and time the medication expires
options.C: The name of the pharmacy supplier
options.D: The manufacturer's original stock number

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients in skin traction?

options.A: Mental fatigue prevents the patient from eating hospital meals
options.B: Anxious patients have higher rates of bone infection than calm ones
options.C: Psychological stress stops the traction weights from pulling correctly

explanation: Being stuck flat in one position is tough on the mind as well as the body. A kind word and clear communication go a long way in nursing care!

question: How is the care for a stable patient with a bruised heart (contusion) different from someone with a bleeding heart wound?

options.A: The blunt injury patient requires immediate open-heart surgery every time.
options.B: The blunt injury patient often receives monitoring and supportive care instead of immediate surgery.
options.C: Medical management is never used for any form of chest trauma.
options.D: Penetrating injuries are always treated with rest and pain medication alone.

explanation: If a patient is stable with a bruised heart, we usually watch them closely in the ICU. But an active stab or gunshot wound? That needs immediate surgery!

question: Which practice is strictly forbidden when handling chemicals in any hospital or lab setting?

options.A: Reading the manufacturer safety sheet before opening the package
options.B: Reporting minor chemical spill near-misses to safety officers
options.C: Transferring chemicals into unlabeled food or drink containers
options.D: Wearing protective gloves and face shields during dilution

explanation: Never put chemicals in old juice or water bottles! Someone could easily mistake it for a drink and suffer accidental poisoning. Always keep containers properly labeled.

question: Why do patients recovering from severe heart trauma need continuous heart rhythm monitoring?

options.A: Rhythm strips are legally required to prove the surgery was successful.

options.C: Damaged heart tissue can trigger dangerous irregular heart rhythms days after the injury.

explanation: Bruised or repaired heart tissue is electrically irritable. Monitoring helps us catch dangerous rhythm changes early and keep our patient safe!

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing barrier methods
options.B: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and seek care
options.C: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never contract another infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel safe and respected without shame, they are honest about their health and more likely to get help.

question: What emergency medicine is given right away after a nurse accidentally pricks their finger with an HIV-contaminated needle?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage
options.B: Antiretroviral maintenance therapy
options.C: Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
options.D: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)

explanation: PEP is taken promptly after a potential exposure to stop the virus before it takes hold. Stay safe out there!

question: Which internal organ is frequently damaged alongside the joints in untreated chronic gout?

options.A: The brain
options.B: The spleen
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The lungs

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual production of milk in the alveoli?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Prolactin

question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation or challenge of healthcare simulation?

options.A: Fitting simulation hours into a packed curriculum is difficult

options.C: Mannequins cannot fully duplicate every emotional nuance of a real patient
options.D: Simulation successfully improves teamwork and reduces medical errors

question: Which of these is a very common complaint from patients suffering from Long COVID?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin
options.B: Chronic fatigue and brain fog
options.C: Sudden bone fractures in the legs
options.D: Uncontrollable weight gain

question: Why are children with acute osteomyelitis at risk for long-term bone growth issues?

options.A: Bones in children never fully heal once inflamed
options.B: Antibiotics used in pediatrics actively dissolve healthy cartilage
options.C: Children lack any ability to form new bone after an infection
options.D: The infection can damage nearby growth plates, altering future bone growth

question: What is a major challenge for injection safety in resource-limited settings like Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive surplus of modern safety-engineered syringes
options.B: Supply chain disruptions and shortages of safety devices
options.C: Complete lack of any national health guidelines or policies
options.D: Patients refusing to accept any injections from trained nurses

explanation: When clinics face stockouts of safety gear and syringes, it makes ideal infection control a tough daily battle for nurses.

question: How can a nurse best stop a child in an oxygen tent from getting chilled by moisture?

options.A: Frequently dry the child's skin and change damp linens
options.B: Turn off the humidifier completely during the night shift
options.C: Apply petroleum jelly over the child's entire body
options.D: Open the canopy wide for one hour every morning

explanation: Regularly swapping out damp clothes and blankets prevents the moisture from chilling the child's body.

question: What is the primary reason nursing pharmacology education became much more rigorous over the past century?

options.A: Patients no longer wanted to take natural remedies.

options.C: Physicians stopped prescribing medications altogether.
options.D: Nurses took over the responsibility of manufacturing hospital drugs.

question: What does 'U=U' (Undetectable = Untransmittable) mean for an HIV-positive person?

options.A: They are completely cured and no longer carry the virus in their body.
options.B: Their blood tests will no longer show any positive antibody results.

question: What is a key nursing action when caring for a patient taking a diuretic medication?

options.A: Check pupil reactions every fifteen minutes
options.B: Accurately monitor intake and output
options.C: Encourage a high-sodium snack diet
options.D: Restrict the patient from walking entirely

question: During the final delivery of the baby's body, which part usually comes out first?

options.A: The posterior hip
options.B: The umbilical cord

options.D: The lower extremities

question: Which of these is NOT a typical barrier to effective nursing counselling?

options.A: Patient mistrust of healthcare workers
options.B: Having too much uninterrupted personal time
options.C: Language and cultural differences
options.D: Severe time constraints in busy clinics

question: Where does a primary health clinic in Nigeria send its monthly injection safety report first?

options.A: The Local Government Area (LGA) focal officer

question: Which medication is the standard, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Atropine

question: Which of these is NOT a red flag symptom that requires medical investigation? (Find the exception)

question: You see a colleague pouring leftover liquid antibiotics down the hospital sink. What is the right nursing response?

options.C: Throw the empty glass bottles into the general household trash bin

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

question: A pregnant patient says she wants to take a random herbal remedy she saw online for her heartburn. What is the nurse's best reply?

question: What is the term for dilated veins in the scrotum that can negatively affect sperm production?

options.C: Hydrocele

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: To restrict patient access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical supervision in rural clinics
options.C: To track service quality, identify gaps, and guide continuous improvement
options.D: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors in patient charts

explanation: You're doing great! Monitoring collects essential data so managers can improve care delivery and patient safety.

question: A patient recovering from near-asphyxiation is cleared to eat, but struggles to swallow properly. Who should you consult?

options.A: A diagnostic radiologist
options.B: A speech-language pathologist
options.C: A hospital pharmacist
options.D: A physical fitness instructor

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at assessing and retraining swallowing safely, keeping patients safe from aspiration pneumonia. Teamwork makes the dream work in healthcare!

question: A newborn is experiencing severe breathing trouble and low oxygen levels. What happens to the blood vessels in the baby's lungs as a result?

options.A: They stop pumping blood back to the right atrium
options.B: They stay constricted, keeping pulmonary resistance high
options.C: They dilate widely to let extra blood flow through
options.D: They turn into permanent fibrous ligaments right away

explanation: Low oxygen causes pulmonary blood vessels to squeeze shut, preventing the normal drop in resistance needed for healthy transition. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h7)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a BP of 220/130 mmHg, chest pain, and confusion. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Normal white coat syndrome
options.B: Isolated systolic hypertension
options.C: Hypertensive urgency
options.D: Hypertensive emergency

explanation: Extremely high blood pressure plus signs of brain or heart distress (like confusion and chest pain) makes this a critical medical emergency. You're crushing these clinical scenarios!

question: What is a major benefit of encouraging male partner involvement in PMTCT programs?

options.A: It improves clinic attendance and supports maternal drug adherence.
options.B: It removes the responsibility of health education from the nurse.
options.C: It allows fathers to breastfeed the infant during the night.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for infant diagnostic testing.

explanation: When male partners are involved and supportive, mothers find it easier to keep appointments and take their medications consistently. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h8)

question: If a primary health care nurse sends a patient to see a mental health specialist, what is this action called?

options.A: Making a referral
options.B: Conducting active listening
options.C: Setting educational goals
options.D: Providing guidance

explanation: When a patient needs specialized care beyond general nursing, connecting them to an expert is called making a referral.

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically confused with a benign cervical ectropion during an exam?

options.A: Uterine fibroids located in the myometrium
options.B: Benign cervical polyps protruding from the os
options.C: Early malignant tumors of the cervix
options.D: Cervicitis caused by sexually transmitted organisms

explanation: Fibroids sit deep inside the muscular wall of the uterus, way past the surface of the cervix, so they won't look like a red patch on the outer cervix. You nailed it!

question: What should you do when a patient's unique situation doesn't quite match standard textbook research?

options.A: Assume the research is completely useless and rely only on guesses
options.B: Use critical thinking to balance the evidence with the patient's individual reality
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately without further assessment
options.D: Ignore the patient's symptoms because the textbook study is always right

explanation: Research gives us a great roadmap, but every patient is unique. As a nurse, you use your critical thinking to adapt care to the person in front of you.

question: Which of these is generally safe and does NOT harm sperm production?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Anabolic steroid abuse
options.C: Elevated scrotal temperature
options.D: Exposure to heavy toxins

explanation: Good news! Regular, moderate exercise keeps your body healthy and balanced. Heat, harsh toxins, and steroids, however, can hurt sperm counts.

question: A patient taking ethambutol reports noticing a change in their vision. What should you do first?

options.A: Report the visual changes promptly to the prescriber.
options.B: Double the next dose of the medication.
options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating green vegetables.
options.D: Reassure the patient that blurry vision is a normal temporary sign.

explanation: Ethambutol can affect the eyes (optic neuritis). Any vision changes need a quick report to the doctor so we can protect the patient's sight!

question: Where does blood go immediately after leaving the right side of the newborn's heart?

options.A: To the lungs
options.B: To the liver
options.C: To the placenta
options.D: To the brain

explanation: The right side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary arteries directly to the lungs for oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: What should you do first if a smart bed's motorized controls stop working?

options.A: Submit a permanent replacement request to hospital administration
options.B: Check the power supply and ensure control lockouts are off
options.C: Immediately transfer the patient to a manual stretcher
options.D: Disassemble the mattress cover to check internal wiring

explanation: Always start with the simple stuff! Check if it's plugged in or if a safety lockout button was accidentally pressed.

question: What is the primary benefit of getting a COVID-19 vaccine?

options.A: Reducing the risk of severe illness and hospitalization
options.B: Curing existing long-term respiratory complications
options.C: Guaranteeing that a person will never catch the virus
options.D: Eliminating the need for hand hygiene and masks

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines train your immune system to fight off the worst parts of the disease, keeping you out of the hospital.

question: Why should nurses be ready to talk about body image and sexual health with GU cancer patients?

options.A: Surgeries and treatments in this area directly affect elimination and sexual health
options.B: Talking about these topics completely eliminates the need for pain medication
options.C: Incontinence and sexual changes only occur in elderly female clients
options.D: Psychological support speeds up the physical regeneration of kidney tissue

explanation: Treatments for these cancers touch some of the most personal parts of a patient's life. Being a compassionate, open listener helps them cope with changes in how their body works.

question: What is a very common challenge for clients after prostate surgery?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to digest proteins
options.B: Chronic infections of the upper respiratory tract
options.C: Urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction
options.D: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck

explanation: Because the prostate sits right next to the nerves and muscles controlling urination and erections, surgery here often causes temporary or lasting trouble with both functions.

question: What is the most helpful advice a nurse can give to a patient who frequently chokes on their food?

options.A: Take a strong sleeping pill before meals to relax
options.B: Cut food into small pieces and avoid talking while chewing
options.C: Drink a large glass of cold water with every bite
options.D: Lie flat on your back right after finishing your meal

explanation: Simple habits make a big difference. Taking small bites, chewing thoroughly, and focusing on your food instead of chatting helps prevent accidental choking.

question: What type of feedback loop does the body mostly use to keep hormone levels balanced?

options.A: Negative feedback loops
options.B: Neutral feedback loops
options.C: External feedback loops
options.D: Positive feedback loops

explanation: Negative feedback is like a home thermostat. When hormone levels get too high, a signal tells the gland to slow down and stop making more until things are balanced again.

question: What are the classic warning signs of peritonitis in a patient getting IP therapy?

options.A: A high fever accompanied by a persistent dry cough
options.B: Sudden swelling and redness of the lower legs
options.C: Cloudy effluent drainage and severe abdominal pain
options.D: Complete inability to speak or swallow food

explanation: Spot on! If the drained fluid looks cloudy instead of clear, paired with bad belly pain, it's a huge red flag for peritonitis (infection). [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is it so vital to write down moulding details accurately on the partograph?

options.A: It proves that the nurse gave pain medication at the correct time
options.B: It replaces the need to check the fetal heart rate during the second stage
options.C: It serves as a legal receipt for the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.D: It gives the healthcare team a clear visual trend of whether labour is becoming obstructed

explanation: The partograph gives everyone a quick visual story of how labour is going, helping the whole shift spot dangerous trends before they become emergencies.

question: A client returns to the ward after having a TURBT (transurethral resection of a bladder tumor). What is your priority nursing check?

options.A: Assessing for bilateral swelling of the lower leg joints
options.B: Checking for sudden changes in visual acuity and hearing
options.C: Monitoring urinary output and watching for bleeding
options.D: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels every two hours

explanation: After bladder surgery, keeping a close eye on their urine through the catheter is vital. We watch for bright red blood or clots so we can catch any bleeding early!

question: Why might a newborn infant have slightly swollen breast tissue shortly after birth?

options.A: Early milk production has begun
options.B: Blockage of the lymphatic vessels
options.C: Maternal hormones crossed the placenta
options.D: A congenital infection of the skin

explanation: High levels of maternal hormones circulate in the baby's blood before birth, causing temporary breast enlargement that soon fades. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is the common medical term for a nosebleed originating from the anterior nasal septum?

options.A: Rhinorrhea
options.B: Anosmia
options.C: Epistaxis
options.D: Sinusitis

explanation: Epistaxis is the clinical term for bleeding from the blood vessels inside the nasal cavity. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which past medical history is most important when assessing a male patient's fertility risks?

options.A: A normal resting heart rate and blood pressure reading
options.B: A history of undescended testicles in childhood
options.C: A personal preference for wearing loose cotton clothing
options.D: Occasional mild muscle soreness after heavy exercise

explanation: Undescended testicles mean the tissue spent time exposed to higher core body heat, which can impact future fertility. Great clinical insight to keep in mind!

question: If a patient has a growth causing uncontrolled hypersecretion of a hormone, what happens?

options.A: Complete shutdown of all nervous system reflex pathways
options.B: An exaggerated physiological response and metabolic disturbance
options.C: Permanent cessation of all tropic hormone production
options.D: Immediate reversal of normal circadian rhythm patterns

explanation: 'Hyper-' means too much! Overproducing hormones puts target organs into overdrive, causing clear signs of imbalance.

question: A mum on her second day after delivery hasn't passed stool and is scared to use the toilet. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withhold all oral fluids and food until she passes flatus
options.B: Administer a strong stimulant enema immediately without consulting a doctor
options.C: Insist that she remains in bed until her bowel movement happens naturally
options.D: Encourage fluid intake, walking around, and check if stool softeners were ordered

explanation: Gentle movement, plenty of fluids, and stool softeners are the safest, kindest way to help her first postpartum toilet trip go smoothly!

question: What is an important long-term instruction for a patient who just received a mechanical heart valve?

options.A: Never drinking pure water again
options.B: Avoiding all forms of physical movement forever
options.C: Stopping daily blood pressure checks at home
options.D: The need for lifelong anticoagulation therapy

explanation: Blood loves to stick to artificial surfaces! Patients with mechanical valves must take blood thinners (anticoagulants) for the rest of their lives to prevent dangerous clots.

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison ulcer
options.B: Cushing's ulcer
options.C: Peptic ulcer
options.D: Curling's ulcer

explanation: Think 'Curling' up from belly pain after a burn! It's a classic stress ulcer caused by low blood flow to the stomach early in shock.

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you realize a medication error has reached a patient?

options.A: Assess the patient's clinical condition and notify the physician
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to see if any symptoms develop
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper inside your uniform pocket
options.D: Resign from your nursing position immediately out of guilt

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. Check on the patient right away and get the doctor's help to manage any unexpected reactions.

question: As a nurse investigator, why is knowing a pathogen's incubation period so helpful when tracing an outbreak?

options.A: It reveals the exact name of the patient who started the outbreak
options.B: It helps calculate the approximate time window when exposure to the source occurred
options.C: It proves whether the infection came from an animal or a human
options.D: It tells the nurse exactly which antibiotic will cure the infection

explanation: Counting backward from when symptoms started using the incubation period helps you pinpoint the exact day the patient likely caught the bug.

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's serum albumin lab result before giving a protein-bound drug?

options.A: To measure the exact body fat percentage
options.B: To see how well the kidneys are making urine
options.C: To determine if there is a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is at risk for drug toxicity

explanation: Low albumin levels change the balance of bound vs. free drug. Checking this lab value helps you keep the patient safe from unexpected high doses of active medicine.

question: What triggers the release of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

options.A: High levels of circulating estrogen
options.B: Emptying of the axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Stretching of Cooper's ligaments
options.D: Infant suckling at the nipple

explanation: Nerve signals from the nipple travel to the brain when a baby suckles, triggering the posterior pituitary to release oxytocin for milk ejection. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h8)

question: What is the main difference between hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Whether the patient is male or female
options.B: The time of day the blood pressure was checked
options.C: The exact numerical value of the diastolic reading
options.D: The presence of acute target organ damage

explanation: Urgency means extremely high pressure, but emergency means the high pressure is actively harming vital organs like the heart or brain. Big difference in how fast we act!

question: What does it mean if a placenta is described as a 'battledore placenta'?

options.A: A placenta with a thick white ring on its edge
options.B: A placenta split into two equal-sized lobes
options.C: A placenta where the umbilical cord inserts at the margin
options.D: A placenta with an accessory lobe nearby

explanation: Think of a battledore insertion like a tennis racket handle attached right at the edge of the disk instead of the middle. Easy to picture once you see it! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h2)

question: If nurses on a ward keep leaving used needles uncapped on trays, what is the best way to fix this habit?

options.A: Issue written warning letters to every single nurse working in the ward
options.B: Ban all injections in the facility until staff members remember the rules
options.C: Conduct training sessions and place safety boxes closer to the point of use
options.D: Wait for the next annual hospital inspection to report the problem

explanation: Making safety gear easy to reach and providing supportive training works much better than punishment for changing clinical habits.

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between a cerebellar intention tremor and a Parkinsonian resting tremor?

options.A: The parkinsonian tremor worsens when reaching for a cup of coffee
options.B: The parkinsonian tremor disappears with rapid alternating movements
options.C: The cerebellar tremor becomes more pronounced as the patient approaches a target
options.D: The cerebellar tremor only appears when the patient is completely asleep

explanation: An intention tremor acts up right as your hand gets close to what it's trying to grab (like reaching for a cup), whereas resting tremors happen when the hands are just sitting still. Perfect nursing assessment knowledge!

question: What causes the glandular tissue of the breast to shrink after menopause?

options.A: Increased activity of Montgomery glands
options.B: Thickening of Cooper's ligaments
options.C: Declining estrogen levels
options.D: Blockage of the lactiferous ducts

explanation: When estrogen levels drop after menopause, glandular tissue regresses and is largely replaced by fat. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h7)

question: Why is addressing psychosocial well-being particularly important for patients with visible, chronic skin conditions?

options.A: Visible skin problems can cause embarrassment, anxiety, and social withdrawal
options.B: Emotional stress directly stops all topical medications from working
options.C: Mental health counseling replaces the need for any physical wound care
options.D: Patients with skin disorders never experience physical pain, only worry

explanation: Chronic and visible dermatological conditions frequently affect body image and self-esteem, making psychological support an important part of holistic care. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h8)

question: What is a key nursing priority when caring for a patient with a new suprapubic catheter after bladder surgery?

options.A: Clamp the drainage tubing tightly every two hours to train the bladder muscles.
options.B: Change the catheter insertion tract daily using dry gauze pads only.
options.C: Ensure the tubing stays unobstructed and check the insertion site for leaking urine or infection.
options.D: Flush the drainage system forcefully with sterile water if urine output slows down.

explanation: Keeping the tube clear and watching the site keeps urine flowing smoothly and stops germs from causing an infection. You've got this nursing routine down!

question: What is the main reason a nursing student is in the operating theatre?

options.A: To administer anaesthetic medications independently
options.B: To replace the scrub nurse during complex procedures
options.C: To act as the primary circulating nurse for major cases
options.D: To learn and observe surgical nursing care firsthand

explanation: As a student, you are there to gain experience, connect your classroom notes to real-life practice, and learn safely under supervision!

question: Why should you warn patients taking regular NSAIDs to steer clear of alcohol?

options.A: It lowers blood sugar to dangerous emergency levels
options.B: It causes immediate and permanent kidney destruction
options.C: It drastically increases the risk of stomach bleeding and ulcers
options.D: It completely stops the pain-relieving action of the drug

explanation: Alcohol and NSAIDs are a harsh double-whammy for the gastric lining. Mixing them together invites nasty stomach irritation and bleeding. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT an expected result of taking a sympathomimetic drug?

options.A: Pupil dilation
options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Increased heart rate
options.D: Decreased heart rate

explanation: Sympathomimetic drugs mimic the sympathetic system—they speed things up, open airways, and widen pupils. They won't slow down the heart rate!

question: Why is it strictly forbidden to use a single-patient lancing device on more than one person?

options.A: It ruins the strip calibration
options.B: It can transmit serious bloodborne infections
options.C: It melts the plastic body of the device
options.D: It causes an internal meter error

explanation: Tiny traces of blood stay on lancing equipment. Sharing devices is a huge infection risk—always use a fresh device per patient!

question: What vital equipment must always be kept ready at the bedside of a patient recovering from an airway issue?

options.A: A standard blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.B: Suction machine and a manual breathing bag
options.C: A sterile surgical tray for major tummy surgery
options.D: An intravenous infusion pump with extra tubing

explanation: Always be prepared! Having suction and a bag-valve-mask right at the bedside lets nurses act instantly if thick mucus blocks the airway or breathing slows down.

question: A new nurse is sorting waste on a busy ward. Which action shows they are following safety rules correctly?

options.A: Dropping a used syringe directly into a puncture-resistant box without recapping
options.B: Tossing blood-stained gauze into the ordinary office waste bin
options.C: Recapping a needle carefully using both hands before disposal
options.D: Storing expired medications in the ward refrigerator next to patient snacks

explanation: Brilliant! Dropping the used syringe straight into the safety box without trying to recap it is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries.

question: Where should used lancets go immediately after a finger prick?

options.A: In the regular trash can
options.B: In a rigid, puncture-proof sharps container
options.C: In the patient's bedside drawer
options.D: In a clean kidney basin to wash later

explanation: Safety first! Used sharps go straight into a puncture-resistant container to protect everyone from accidental sticks.
